name: emporix
_readme: Emporix as a TARGET only: multi-tenant, API-first, B2B-native composable commerce SaaS with no shipped frontend and no CMS - services are consumed a la carte over the Emporix Commerce API and extended through webhooks/events and external services. Seed from the vendor's service list; the API paths are a best-effort reconstruction of the documented service shape and must be verified against developer.emporix.io before use. No source role, no adapter.py.

as_target.default_frontend: none shipped - headless, bring your own frontend (Emporix offers storefront starters/accelerators, verify their status and licence)

snippets.critic2_persona: senior solution architect who has delivered B2B commerce on Emporix as well as on an established enterprise platform, and who is deliberately sceptical about a young ecosystem - insisting on a documentation URL or a reference for every capability claim rather than accepting the vendor's feature list
snippets.docs_domains: developer.emporix.io (the developer portal: service-by-service guides, the API reference per service, tenant and site configuration, mixins/schema, events and webhooks, authentication) and the OpenAPI references it links for each service on api.emporix.io; emporix.com for product and packaging statements (treat as marketing, not as a contract); the Emporix documentation is thinner than that of the large vendors - documentation depth is a reported weakness - so expect to confirm behaviour with vendor support or a proof of concept and record WHO confirmed it and when. Never cite a remembered path: service names and paths must come from the current API reference.
snippets.best_practice: consume only the services the solution needs and keep the rest of the stack replaceable - that is the platform's own premise; model B2B structure with the platform's primitives (company/legal-entity accounts, contacts, approval configuration, price lists and contract prices, cost centres) before adding custom fields; extend entities through mixins (schema-registered JSON extensions) rather than by inventing parallel storage, so the data stays queryable and validated; drive integration by events/webhooks with idempotent consumers instead of polling; keep tenant and site configuration in the configuration/site-settings services rather than hard-coding it in the frontend; treat pricing, availability and tax as service calls with explicit caching decisions, because a B2B storefront with contract prices cannot be cached the way a B2C catalog can; put any logic the platform does not offer in an own service and keep the contract narrow enough that the platform stays upgradable.
snippets.critic2_focus: D1: which services and features actually exist in the tenant's subscription, what is GA versus roadmap, and what the current service and path names are (this platform's naming has moved) - demand a developer.emporix.io URL. D2: is the claimed capability a documented service feature or a customisation the vendor demonstrated once. D3: does the service really cover the requirement including the BACK-OFFICE side (the management UI a business user needs), and is there a reference customer at comparable scale. D4: exact service paths and payloads, event/webhook coverage for the required integrations, mixin behaviour for every custom attribute, and for content requirements which external CMS supplies the component.
snippets.expected_hotspots_d3: content, landing pages and navigation of any kind (no CMS - see content_model_notes); back-office depth for CSR, order management and merchandising staff; B2C features, which are lighter than the B2B side (rich promotions, loyalty, wishlist/gift registry, ratings and reviews, marketing automation hooks); search and faceting quality on large catalogs; complex product structures (configurable products, made-to-order, bundles, units of measure and packaging conversions); tax determination beyond the shipped tax service; returns, credit notes and invoice documents; payment method breadth per market; reporting and analytics, which is an external concern; PIM depth for large assortments even though the platform has PIM capabilities
snippets.expected_blockers_d4: young ecosystem and small market presence: fewer public reference customers, fewer implementation partners and thinner documentation than the incumbents, so estimates carry more discovery risk and vendor dependency - all of these are reported weaknesses to validate; less proven at very large scale, so catalog size, order throughput and peak behaviour need a load reference or a proof of concept rather than a datasheet number; no shipped frontend, so the storefront, SSR/caching, SEO and URL model are entirely the project's own build; no CMS, so every content component needs an external CMS plus a binding layer plus a renderer; a smaller extension marketplace means capabilities that are apps elsewhere become custom services here; multi-tenant SaaS means no server-side extension point inside the platform - custom logic runs beside it, with the latency and consistency cost that implies; event/webhook delivery guarantees, retry behaviour and ordering must be verified before an integration depends on them; API rate limits and quotas per tenant must be verified; data migration paths for historical orders and customer credentials must be verified per service
snippets.content_model_notes: Emporix ships NO CMS. The documented service list is commerce-side (product information, price and tax, cart and checkout, order management, customer management, inventory, promotions) with no page, template, slot or block resource *(verify against the current service catalogue)*. The content-shaped primitives that do exist are the media/asset service for images and documents, localized texts on products and categories, mixins (schema-registered JSON extensions) for additional structured fields, and the label/configuration services for localized UI strings and per-site settings *(verify each)*. Consequence for a fit estimation: every content, landing-page, banner and navigation requirement is external CMS work plus a binding layer plus a renderer in the project's own frontend - three distinct pieces, never covered-standard. Record which CMS the target architecture names before estimating any content requirement.
snippets.api_families_hint: see knowledge target_api_endpoint_families - one REST surface per tenant on api.emporix.io, composed of independent services, with the tenant in the path and OAuth2 client-credential tokens; the paths in the knowledge list are a best-effort reconstruction and every one of them must be confirmed against the current API reference before it is quoted in a deliverable
